lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet is the right word for this franchise right now - and that's not a complaint. The Leafs are in the deep offseason, with camp still ahead and the real work now sitting in roster math, not box scores. The most interesting wrinkle is the churn at the margins: a few PTO invites have already turned into NHL contracts, the kind of business that can harden a bottom-six group without costing a fortune. Jake McCabe remains the kind of defender who gives this club a spine, and any honest 2026-27 plan starts with asking how much more he can carry at 32. Auston Matthews is still the standard-bearer, still the tone-setter - the notebook piece makes that plain. The Leafs finished last season and now the question is simpler: who sticks when camp opens? That battle, not nostalgia, will tell the story in September.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: A sloppy finish in Sacramento has sharpened the Jays' offseason mood - less celebration, more triage. The walk-off, 6-5 loss to the Athletics put a bright light on the same old problems: shaky defence, loose control of the running game, and a bullpen that couldn't seal the door. Toronto sits at 70-71, and that final number matters now only as a warning label, not a badge. The real story is health and reinforcements. Anthony Santander is finally headed to Buffalo for a rehab assignment, while Jameson Taillon's elbow has the club bracing for a lost season. That leaves John Schneider and the front office to sort out who belongs in the 2027 core and who is merely passing through. Watch Santander's ramp-up, Taillon's prognosis, and every roster move that follows.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet is a dangerous sound around this franchise, because it means the heavy lifting is happening offstage. The biggest wrinkle is the Kawhi Leonard situation still hasn't been buttoned up - a move that has hovered over Toronto's summer and now hangs over the roster like a judge's gavel. That's the headline, and it matters because the Raptors are trying to sort out a team that finished 0-0-0? No - season over, and that's the point: now the work is construction, not rescue. Scottie Barnes remains the engine, Jakob Poeltl remains the hinge, and the question is whether Toronto has enough shooting and enough certainty to make the pieces fit. Training camp is next, and this front office has to turn rumor into a real rotation.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A roster that finally looks healthier has given Washington a pulse heading into Philadelphia - nothing more, nothing less. Dan Quinn said everybody participated in Monday's walkthrough, a welcome sign after a messy August, and that matters because this club cannot afford a slow start with Jayden Daniels still the engine and Terry McLaurin still the standard. The Commanders spent the offseason adding Stefon Diggs for juice and sorting through the fallout at left tackle, where Laremy Tunsil's injury forced a hard reset. At 0-0, the record is clean; the ledger is not. But health, for once, is bending their way. Watch the right side of the line, the edge rotation, and whether this new-look group can survive opening night in Philadelphia.

article.title: Tuesday's Skate
paragraphs: Jake McCabe sits near the center of the Leafs story this morning, with one look ahead asking what a successful 2026-27 season should look like for him, while another piece points to Auston Matthews setting the tone in camp coverage. For the Blue Jays, the latest note is a bitter one, with a rally ending in walk-off heartbreak as Dylan Cease and the defense stumbled.

The Raptors are still in deep offseason mode, with fresh takes sorting through the good, the bad and the ugly for 2026-27, plus staff reactions to the Kawhi Leonard news.
